Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
931 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Advisories issued through Thursday afternoon for
an extended period of minor tidal flooding.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures are expected
  through early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures are expected
through early next week.

Surface high pressure continues to build north of the forecast area
through the end of the week, yielding dry conditions, seasonal 
temperatures, and limited cloud cover. High temperatures will be
in the 60s to near 70s each day with overnight lows in the 30s to
mid 40s. 

High pressure will build southward out of southeastern Canada and 
eastern Great Lakes region Saturday through Tuesday. Dry conditions 
are expected each day. There could be some areas of frost Saturday 
morning. Temperatures will start out chilly Saturday with highs 5 to 
7 degrees below average and highs generally in the upper 50s to 
lower 60s. By Sunday, temperatures will be more seasonable. Monday 
will encounter highs approaching or reaching the 70 degree mark. By 
Tuesday, temperatures may be knocked down to seasonable once again. 
Highs in the middle 60s.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions continue as surface high pressure builds overhead
and dry conditions persist. Winds remain primarily out of the
north today before shifting to northwesterly on Thursday. On
Friday, winds shift to northeasterly. Terminals located near the
I-95 corridor will gust around 15 knots each afternoon. 
Otherwise, terminals can expect light northerly winds, no 
precipitation, and VFR conditions. 

VFR conditions Saturday through Sunday night. Winds light and 
variable through the period.

&&

.MARINE...
The Nor'easter off the Mid-Atlantic coast will deliver a 
prolonged period of SCA conditions (mainly over the 
central/lower waters). Small Craft Advisories remain in effect
and will likely need to be extended. The threat is highest in 
the lower portions of the waters, with additional Advisories 
possible through the end of the week. Otherwise, dry conditions 
and non-hazardous marine weather is expected. 

No marine hazards expected Saturday through Sunday night. Winds 
light and variable through the period.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
A Nor'easter will continue to circulate offshore through
Thursday as high pressure builds to our north. This will lead to
persistent northerly flow over the waters. Elevated tide levels
are expected through the week as we approach the Full Moon on
Oct 26. Minor tidal flooding is forecast at Annapolis, Dahlgren,
and Solomons Island where Coastal Flood Advisories have been
issued through Thursday afternoon's high tide cycle. These are
likely to be extended and some other locations may also need
Advisories. 

&&
